prototypeScope: V1.8 head and torso rebuild on top of the printed V1.6/V1.7 set: White face plate with direct camera screws, Yellow lower head shell without the beak-roof window and with the upper lip, Yellow jaw frame with the lower lip, Orange head cap with the Pi rails 1 mm higher, Black eye trim with the two camera screw pilots, plus the Orange rear electronics pack and its Black cover that replace the power support, OpenRB tray, fuse bank, regulator insert and IMU clamp/cover, and the Black 4.9 mm neck pitch ring with optional 1 mm and 2 mm shims. Every other printed part stays.
knownFitBoundary: Camera: two M2 x 8 TAP screws from behind the board into the eye-trim pilots; the side holes sit on the face pegs. Pi: three M2 x 6 and one M2 x 4 (E-pi-02) into the cap rails as in V1.7, seats 1 mm higher. Physical checks remain: ribbon dressing at the camera connector, cap closing with the plugged jumper housings, and the pack slide-in behind the hip-yaw motors.
processOverrideReason: Head cap tip angle 9.0 degrees is below the 10 degree line in guide/print/orientation-study/PRINT-ORIENTATION-PRACTICE.md; 3 to 5 mm brim.

parts.changeReason: V1.8 lower head shell: the V1.6 shell with the square beak-roof window filled completely (the raised Pi no longer needs it), and the upper lip pad (source p.obj / ID40) printed as part of the shell instead of being glued in after closing, which had covered the two front closure screws; a 5.2 mm driver hole runs through the lip under each front screw. Geometry outside the window box and the pad seat is identical to V1.6 (print/head-bottom-strip/close_strip.json, print/head-bottom-pad/merge_pad.json).

parts.poseOrigin: 10/1 batch jaw frame pose (copy-manifest object 14, community-4.stl), recovered by registering that print mesh to the source jaw (vertex-identical, residual 1e-8); the source frame is the same robot frame
parts.changeReason: V1.8 jaw frame: the 10/1 jaw frame (source 4.obj / ID4) with the lower lip pad (source q.obj / ID42) printed as part of it instead of glued into its pocket, so no joint in the beak is glued and the whole beak is yellow. A 0.9 mm bridge inset 1.5 mm inside the pad outline ties the pad bottom to the pocket floor; geometry outside the pad box is identical to the 10/1 jaw (print/jaw-pad/merge_jaw_pad.json). The pad underside at the two back corners of the lip prints over low support 1.7 to 3 mm above the bed.

parts.sourceFrame: robot frame (mm, x forward, y left, z up)

parts.changeReason: V1.8 face plate: flat 1.3 mm plate only. Four camera bearing lands, two locating pegs and two 2.2 mm screw holes for the direct camera mount; the inherited corner bosses, eye bosses, oval slot, clamp anchors and two blind pockets are removed or filled, and the three 0.58 mm pits the old clamp pilots left in the back face are filled flat (print/face-pits/fill_pits.json).

parts.sourceFrame: robot frame (mm, x forward, y left, z up)
parts.poseOrigin: V1.6/V1.7 cap flat pose expressed in the robot frame: worldToFlatPrint = sourceToPrint @ worldToStlFrame from candidates/head-cap-pi-shift/manifest.json (same 104.39 mm2 bed contact and bounds)
parts.changeReason: V1.8 head cap: the V1.7 cap (Pi seat 4.6 mm back, +y rail trimmed) with both Pi rails raised 1.0 mm so the plugged jumper housings clear the lower shell without a beak window, and the two unused rear roof bosses removed. The four audio roof posts (two speaker-cage bosses, two amplifier posts) are removed too: the speaker and amplifier are deferred to a later loose add-on (cap-no-audio/remove_audio_posts.py). Outer skin identical to V1.6.

supportBlockers.reason: Keep the +y upper Pi pilot (E-pi-04) free of internal support; the V1.6 Bambu slice put 15 support segments in it. Moved with the rails (+1 mm z over V1.7). Non-printing slicer modifier, robot frame.
Keep the two zip-tie slots of the rear cable notch free of support in the flat pose (V1.6 pose-0 slice put 851 support samples there). Robot-frame copy of the V1.6 blocker; the notch is unchanged.

parts.changeReason: V1.8 rear electronics pack: hangs on the four existing hip-yaw case screws in place of the integrated power support and holds the OpenRB-150 upright on four pads, the DFR1202 in a channel behind it and the BNO085 on its front plate (no junction pocket: the servos take power through the OpenRB ports). Replaces the power support, the regulator insert, the OpenRB tray, the fuse bank and the IMU clamp/cover; no fuses.

At 4.9 mm it touches both faces, like the working hip-yaw rings. ID 16.4 and OD 22 unchanged (print/neck-ring/thicken_ring.py).
